module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 944

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/944](https://www.erdosproblems.com/944)
-/

@[expose] public section

universe u
variable {V : Type u}

namespace Erdos944

open Erdos944

/--
The predicate that graph $G$ with chromatic number $k$ is such that every vertex is critical, yet
every critical set of edges has size $>r$
-/
def SimpleGraph.IsErdos944 (G : SimpleGraph V) (k r : ℕ) : Prop :=  G.IsCritical k ∧
    (∀ (edges : Set (Sym2 V)), G.IsCriticalEdges edges → r < edges.ncard)

/--
Let $k \ge 4$ and $r\ge 1$. Must there exist a graph $G$ with chromatic number $k$
 such that every vertex is critical, yet every critical set of edges has size $>r$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_944 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 4, ∀ r ≥ 1, ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 k r := by
  sorry

/--
Let $k \ge 4$. Must there exist a graph $G$ with chromatic number $k$
such that every vertex is critical, yet every critical set of edges has size $>1$?

This was conjectured by Dirac in 1970.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 4, ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 k 1 := by
  sorry


/--
Dirac's conjecture was proved, for $k=5$: There exists a graph $G$ with chromatic number $5$, such
that every vertex is critical, yet every critical set of edges has size $>1$, or in other words:
has no critical edge.

[Br92] Brown, Jason I., A vertex critical graph without critical edges. Discrete Math. (1992), 99--101
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_eq_5 :
    ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 5 1 := by
  sorry

/--
Lattanzio [La02] proved there exist $k$-critical graphs without critical edges for all $k$ such that
$k - 1$ is not prime.

[La02] Lattanzio, John J., A note on a conjecture of {D}irac. Discrete Math. (2002), 323--330
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_sub_one_not_prime (k : ℕ) (hk : 4 ≤ k)
    (h : ¬ (k - 1).Prime) : ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 k 1 := by
  sorry

/--
Jensen [Je02] gave an construction for $k$-critical graphs without any critical edges for all $k ≥ 5$.

[Je02] Jensen, Tommy R., Dense critical and vertex-critical graphs. Discrete Math. (2002), 63--84.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_ge_five (k : ℕ) (hk : 5 ≤ k) :
    ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 k 1 := by
  sorry

/--
The case $k=4$ and $r=1$ was the remaining open case: Are there $4$-critical graphs
without any critical edges?

Answer: Yes. The Lean formalization linked below proves the existence of such a graph.
Together with Jensen's result for $k \ge 5$, this settles Dirac's conjecture for every
$k \ge 4$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/erdos-944-dirac-k4-lean/blob/9606d77/lean4web/Erdos944K4R1Lean4Web.lean#L676-L690"]
theorem erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_eq_four :
    answer(True) ↔ ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 4 1 := by
  sorry

/--
Martinsson and Steiner [MaSt25] proved for every $r \ge 1$ if $k$ is sufficiently large, depending
on $r$, there exist a graph $G$ with chromatic number $k$ such that every vertex is critical,
yet every critical set of edges has size $>r$.

[MaSt25] Martinsson, Anders and Steiner, Raphael, Vertex-critical graphs far from edge-criticality. Combin. Probab. Comput. (2025), 151--157
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_944.variants.large_k_for_any_r (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) : ∀ᶠ k in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 k r := by
  sorry

  end Erdos944

findings.description: All seven theorems carry `@[category ..., AMS 11]` (AMS 11 = Number theory). Erdős 944 is a graph-colouring problem: vertex-critical graphs and critical edge sets. Its classification is AMS 05 (Combinatorics, 05C15 Coloring of graphs). Every other chromatic-number Erdős file in the repository (e.g. 23, 57, 63, 74, 87, 920–923, 1175) uses `AMS 5`. The Lean mathematics is unaffected; this is a metadata slip only.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/944 tags the problem "graph theory | chromatic number" (Wayback snapshot 2026-07-09). teorth/erdosproblems data/problems.yaml gives tags: ["graph theory", "chromatic number"] for 944.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `AMS 11` by `AMS 5` in all seven `@[category ...]` attributes.

reformulations.difference: The source is about (finite) graphs and critical sets of edges of G. The Lean lets the vertex type `V` be arbitrary, possibly infinite. It quantifies over every `edges : Set (Sym2 V)`, which may contain non-edges and diagonal elements. It measures size with `Set.ncard`, which is 0 on infinite sets. This affects every theorem in the file, since they all state `∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 k r`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (i) A set S is critical iff S ∩ G.edgeSet is critical (Mathlib `deleteEdges_eq_inter_edgeSet`). For finite V, |S ∩ E| ≤ |S|, so 'every critical S : Set (Sym2 V) has ncard > r' is equivalent to 'every critical S ⊆ E(G) has size > r'. (ii) `G.IsCritical k` with k ≥ 1 forces V to be finite. Since χ(G) = k, de Bruijn–Erdős compactness (Mathlib `nonempty_hom_of_forall_finite_subgraph_hom`) gives a finite subgraph H that is not (k−1)-colourable. A vertex v outside H would have χ(G − v) ≥ k, so v would not be critical. Hence, for k ≥ 1, `∃ V G, G.IsErdos944 k r` holds iff some finite graph is k-vertex-critical with no critical edge set of size ≤ r. That is the source's statement. Proved in Lean in /workspace/review/reform.lean: `Review.edges_reform`, `Review.finite_of_isCritical` (both universe-polymorphic) and `Review.exists_reform`. All depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/944 (live site behind a Cloudflare challenge; read via http://web.archive.org/web/20260709214459/https://www.erdosproblems.com/944)

review.notes:
No misformalizations found; the only finding is the AMS 11 metadata slip.

What each declaration was checked against:
- `erdos_944` matches erdosproblems.com/944 word for word: "Let k≥4 and r≥1. Must there exist a graph G with chromatic number k such that every vertex is critical, yet every critical set of edges has size >r?". The answer slot has the same polarity as the question. `research open` agrees with the source, and k = 4 with r ≥ 2 is still open.
- `dirac_conjecture` states Dirac's conjecture, the r = 1 case for all k ≥ 4.
- `k_eq_5` is Brown 1992.
- `k_sub_one_not_prime` is Lattanzio 2002. Skottova–Steiner state it as "all k ≥ 4 such that k−1 is not prime"; Martinsson–Steiner write k ≥ 5, which is the same since 3 is prime. The hypothesis `4 ≤ k` is necessary: at k = 2, K2 has a critical edge.
- `k_ge_five` is Jensen 2002.
- `large_k_for_any_r` is Martinsson–Steiner, Theorem 1.1: "For every r there is k0 such that for every k ≥ k0 ...".

Sanity checks in Lean (/workspace/review/k4test.lean): K4 is 4-chromatic, but deleting s(0,1) makes it 3-colourable, so `¬ IsErdos944 K4 4 1`. The edge condition therefore has real content. The external witness below shows the predicate can also be satisfied.

The `k_eq_four` status and formal_proof record hold. The linked proof is a 48-vertex, 6-regular Cayley graph on S4 × C2 with kernel-checked colouring certificates. I compiled it against the repository's own definitions: I removed its copied definitions and imported `FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«944»` (/workspace/review/extproof.lean). The result `True ↔ ∃ V G, Erdos944.SimpleGraph.IsErdos944 G 4 1` depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. A separate C backtracking check of the same graph agrees: G is not 3-colourable but is 4-colourable, every G−v is 3-colourable, and none of the 144 graphs G−e is 3-colourable. So `answer(True)` / `research solved` is correct for `k_eq_four`, and, together with Jensen, for `dirac_conjecture`.

The newest erdosproblems.com snapshot I could read (2026-07-09) still says "the case k=4 and r=1 remains open". The file changed on 2026-09-21 (local git log only; I did not use GitHub). The file is ahead of the source, not stale, so I filed no status issue.

A variant that could be added: Skottova–Steiner (arXiv:2508.08703) prove that (k,r)-graphs exist for all k ≥ 5 and r ≥ 1, and that f_k(n) = Ω(n^{1/3}). This subsumes `k_ge_five` and `large_k_for_any_r`. Erdős's quantitative form, f_k(n) → ∞, is not formalized.

The primary papers of Brown, Lattanzio and Jensen are paywalled (ScienceDirect returned 403). Their results are described the same way in erdosproblems.com and in both arXiv papers above, which is why I consider them settled.
